candidates.title: WorkFactory: Turning Professional Intents into Executable Work for Scalable Agent Training
candidates.content: Scaling supervised training for working agents requires diverse professional tasks that yield reliable expert demonstrations. However, missing or inconsistent task information can obstruct teacher execution and weaken the resulting supervision. We propose WorkFactory, a scalable framework for constructing coherent and executable professional tasks. Starting from professional intents, information-level planning builds an information support graph to guide task instantiation, explicitly representing the dependencies and locations of information required for the intended outputs. Probe executions then identify support failures and guide repairs while preserving the intended work. We construct 112,686 tasks spanning 612 occupations and use the collected teacher trajectories to fine-tune Qwen models at 4B, 27B, and 35B-A3B scales, yielding the WorkPilot family. All three models improve over their respective base models across four professional-work benchmarks, with WorkPilot-35B-A3B improving from 879 to 1565 Elo on GDPval-AA v2.1. candidates.title: PreView: Enhancing GUI Grounding with Preprocessed Views and Cues
candidates.content: GUI grounding requires locating small controls in cluttered screenshots and identifying which control a natural-language instruction refers to. Cropping and enlargement can expose local detail, but the resulting image may still leave ambiguity about the intended target. We propose PreView, an auxiliary preprocessor that improves the inputs to an existing grounding model without further training that model. PreView prepares two complementary types of input features: task-relevant views for localization and candidate-specific cues for target understanding. A trained lightweight auxiliary model predicts and refines a center, crops the screenshot into a local view, and enlarges that view for zoomed-in grounding. It also prepares a visual cue (i.e., a red-circle marker with a location hint) and a textual cue describing the candidate's identity or function. The frozen grounding model uses the prepared inputs to predict the final click. Across five benchmarks, PreView improves the average grounding accuracy of Qwen3-VL-2B, OS-Atlas-4B, and Qwen3-VL-4B without further training these grounding models. candidates.title: PersonaCUABench: Benchmarking Computer-Use Agents Serving Diverse Personas
candidates.content: Computer-use agents (CUAs) are commonly evaluated against fixed task specifications, but users may omit requirements, add constraints, or require approval before consequential actions. Completing the benchmark instruction does not guarantee serving the person who asked. We introduce PersonaCUABench, which holds 74 tasks across 11 domains fixed and varies only who asks. A persona agent, playing one of 44 personas in four groups, rewrites each instruction in that user's own words and answers the CUA's questions, while the CUA sees only the dialogue, never the profile or the original instruction. Across nine backbones (3,330 runs), mean task completion falls by 36% relative to the original requests. The losses have two sources: in 59.9% of cells that lose points, the agent engages with what the user asked for and still gets it wrong, and 11.2% are stops the user requested that the checker scores as failures. Even when a persona request is fully completed, the user gives the top satisfaction rating in only 62.7% of cells, against 84.1% for the original requests. CUAs should therefore be evaluated not only on task completion but also on whether they meet the requirements and constraints

candidates.content: How I Built the Most AI-Pilled Company in the World Don't be put off by the clickbait headline, this piece by Jacob Sansbury describing how they are building Spawn is a fascinating exploration of the bleeding edge of what's possible with agentic engineering against frontier models. Spawn is a massively multiplayer gaming environment where players can use prompts (to the in-game agent, Savi) to modify the game world. I fired it up on my phone for a few minutes and was able to prompt a castle into existence, then a dragon, then ride the dragon to fly around that castle. By Jacob's telling, Spawn is now being developed autonomously by a swarm of Fable-powered agents costing over $3 million in tokens per month ("we spend 30x payroll on AI tokens"). candidates.title: Metal-ion coordination drives active-site remodeling for backsplicing in circularly permuted group II introns
candidates.content: Abstract Circularly permuted (CP) group II introns are self-splicing ribozymes that undergo a sequential branching and backsplicing reaction to yield branched introns and circular exons (circRNAs). While the initial branching step is structurally characterized, the mechanistic principles that govern the subsequent large-scale active-site remodeling and stringent metal-ion specificity required for backsplicing remain poorly understood. Here, we present a series of high-resolution cryo-EM structures of the CP group II intron from Gluconacetobacter diazotrophicus PAL5 ( Gdi -1), capturing the ribozyme at discrete stages along the branching -to- backsplicing pathway under distinct ionic conditions. Comparative analyses under K + /Mg 2+ , K + /Ca 2+ , and Cs + /Mg 2+ conditions demonstrate that productive backsplicing relies on ion-specific coordination networks that govern 3′ splice site (3′SS) docking and catalytic center formation, revealing the precise metal-ion-coordinated conformational rearrangements and dynamic splice-site exchange mechanisms. candidates.title: Biobank-scale self-supervised genotype pretraining yields transferable representations for human genetics
candidates.content: Abstract Biobank-scale genotyping has created unprecedented cohorts for human genetics, yet the field still lacks scalable methods for learning transferable representations from largely unlabeled individual-level genotype data. Here, we introduce SNPBERT, a self-supervised transformer pretrained on genotypes from 485 923 UK Biobank participants using masked rsID prediction. SNPBERT embeddings recovered known population structure across UK Biobank and three external datasets, performed comparably to principal component analysis, and supported the identification of ancestry-informative marker SNPs. Fine-tuning with an attention-based multiple-instance head generated disease-specific risk scores that provided complementary information beyond conventional polygenic risk scores. The relative increase in Nagelkerke’s R 2 ranged from 0.7% to 3.3%, and independent associations were observed for seven of the eight chronic diseases examined. In celiac disease, attention prioritization recapitulated major histocompatibility complex signals while elevating variants in CCHCR1 and NOTCH4 relative to genome-wide association study (GWAS) ranking. candidates.title: The Mycobacterium tuberculosis Ku C-terminus orchestrates LigD activity through domain-specific interactions
candidates.content: Abstract Bacterial non-homologous end joining (NHEJ) is a key DNA double-strand break (DSB) repair pathway that relies on the Ku–LigD complex to alleviate genomic instability. The Mycobacterium tuberculosis Ku C-terminus has been highlighted for its role in LigD recruitment to DSBs and stimulation of LigD ligase activity. However, it remains unclear how the Ku C-terminus interacts with and potentially influences other LigD activities. Here, we combine NMR spectroscopy, structural modelling, and mutational analysis to define the interaction interface between the Ku C-terminus and LigD. We identify critical residues in Ku (E246, V248, S258, K260, and N266) and the LigD polymerase (D162, V194, R198) and ligase (D522, K579, L580) domains that mediate this interaction. Functional assays reveal that Ku stimulates LigD ligase activity through contacts with both polymerase and ligase domains, while Ku attenuates template-dependent polymerase activity, contrasting previous studies in Pseudomonas aeruginosa homologs. candidates.title: Yeast surface display reveals structure-dependent β-glucan association with the plant immune receptor AtIGP1
candidates.content: Cell wall-derived oligosaccharides can function as immune-active signals in plants and trigger pattern-triggered immunity (PTI) through pattern recognition receptors (PRRs). In Arabidopsis thaliana, the leucine-rich repeat malectin (LRR-MAL) receptor kinase IGP1 (impaired in glycan perception 1) contributes to immune responses induced by cellulose- and mixed-linkage {beta}-1,3/1,4-glucan (MLG)-derived oligosaccharides, although whether MLG-derived oligosaccharides are directly recognized by AtIGP1 needs further clarification. We established a Saccharomyces cerevisiae surface-display system in which the AtIGP1 extracellular domain (ECD) is presented at the yeast cell surface, allowing oligosaccharide recognition to be examined separately from downstream plant signaling and without receptor purification. Previously, cellulose-derived oligosaccharides have been shown to elicit plant defense responses via AtIGP1. Here, surface-displayed AtIGP1 retained the ability to recognize fluorescently labeled cellotriose (CEL3) and cellopentaose (CEL5) ligands, supporting functional presentation of the receptor for investigating glycan recognition in a heterologous context. candidates.title: NanoPro - a Framework for Probiotically-Guided Nanovector Therapy
candidates.content: The 'antigen problem', i.e. the disconnect between the broad spectrum of therapeutic modes enabled by the range of viral and synthetic nanoparticles for which workable receptor-targeting architectures exist and the relative dearth of addressable target receptors on most tumors, is a long-standing challenge in targeted tumor nanotherapy. Here we provide in vitro-proof-of-principle for NanoPro, a platform for guiding nanoscale therapeutics to otherwise antigenically indistinct tumors via probiotically-released tumor cell-binding tags, ProTags. These consist of an orthogonal antigen (GFP or ALFA) fused to the heparin-binding domain of placenta growth factor-2 and serve as attachment receptors for ProTag-targeted nanovectors. ProTag release from Escherichia coli Nissle 1917 was facilitated by deletion of the membrane-tethering lpp gene, which increased ProTag supernatant concentrations 16.5-fold compared to the parental strain without impacting viability. candidates.content: [NA] RECRUITING | 申办方/赞助方: Fred Hutchinson Cancer Center | 适应症: Human Papillomavirus-Related Carcinoma. This clinical trial compares usual care to interpersonal communication training and vaccination workflow training, alone or in combination, for improving communication about and recommendations for human papillomavirus (HPV) and other vaccinations in pharmacies. Low HPV vaccination in the United States has placed unvaccinated children at risk of developing cancers as adults that could have been prevented. Pharmacies can be convenient for vaccination because they are open longer hours, have shorter wait times, can see patients without appointments and may cost less. However, many people are not aware that vaccination is available in pharmacies and some pharmacies lack the commitment from staff to vaccinate or may not have protocols in place for vaccination. Proactive communication approaches to recommending HPV vaccination have been shown to be effective in medical offices but have not been tested in the pharmacy setting. candidates.title: [Correspondence] Global health reform: a suggestion

candidates.title: Licensure Framework for Autonomous Clinical Artificial Intelligence
candidates.content: To the Editor The authors of a recent Perspective article proposed requiring autonomous clinical AI systems to score at or above the median of human test takers’ scores on the US Medical Licensing Examination and relevant specialty board examinations. The call for staged authorization is welcome, but this particular threshold asks written examinations to do something they were not designed to do: determine whether a system is ready to manage patients without per-case clinician review.

candidates.title: AI-Powered Clinical Decision Support Tools

Additional risks arise when the AI technology itself is designed to advance commercial interests. However, bias must be avoided to prevent commercial interests, including pharmaceutical, device, and diagnostic testing companies, from affecting medical judgment and influencing prescribing.

candidates.title: TradeStation Europe expands operations capability
candidates.content: TradeStation Europe B.V. (“TradeStation Europe”), the recently licensed European brokerage subsidiary of TradeStation Group, Inc. (“TradeStation”), today announced a round of product updates, including extended-hours options trading, along with reduced options and equities pricing, new single-stock option spreads and expanded intraday trading to enhance the offering for retail and institutional traders across the Netherlands and the European Economic Area (EEA).

candidates.title: Canton Foundation backs RedStone to build pricing standard
candidates.content: RedStone, the data layer for institutional DeFi, today announced that the Canton Foundation has unanimously approved funding through the Canton Development Fund to develop the Canton Access and Privacy Standard (CAPS), an open-source framework for institutional market-data infrastructure on Canton. CAPS is designed to let institutions price transactions on Canton without revealing their underlying positions or agreed settlement values to data providers.

candidates.title: Liquidity Services deploys Flywire tech for domestic and cross-border B2B payments
candidates.content: Flywire Corporation (Nasdaq: FLYW), a global payments enablement and software company, today announced that Liquidity Services Inc. (Nasdaq: LQDT) has implemented Flywire to run both domestic and cross-border B2B payments for the global e-commerce marketplace, with over $15 billion in total completed transactions over the course of Liquidity Services International's 25 year history.

candidates.title: Directional Statistics on Circles and Spheres: A New Angle on Data
candidates.content: arXiv:2610.36227v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Two compass bearings near north can have an ordinary arithmetic mean pointing south: the difficulty is that angles live on a circle, not a straight line. Using real wind observations, diffusion-MRI orientations, and geometric examples from machine learning, this article introduces circular and axial averages, directional variability, and probability models on circles and spheres. The guiding principle is to identify the geometry and symmetries of the observations before choosing a statistical method.
